references.text: The original command on how the breastplate was to be attached to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it would stay fastened over the ephod's belt.
Detailed instructions on how the breastplate was to be made and attached to the ephod with gold rings and a blue cord.
The introduction to the chapter describing the making of the holy garments from blue, purple, and crimson wool, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The description of how the breastplate was made from the same materials as the ephod.
The original command to make the ephod to which the breastplate was to be attached.
Another use of a blue cord (petil tekhelet) in the priestly garments, namely to attach the holy diadem to the turban.
A parallel mechanism (blue cord for attaching holy objects) showing unified obedience for both the turban and the breastplate.
